Performing initial audit of PKGBUILD to ensure that we can safely run `makepkg`
LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a single source for x86_64: a Debian package downloaded from the project's official GitHub releases page over HTTPS. The URL is constructed using the tagged version and is hosted at `github.com/nkzw-tech/codiff`, which matches the project's stated upstream. There are no command substitutions, obfuscated expressions, or remote code executions in the global scope or within `pkgver()`. The `pkgver()` function is absent, so version computation relies solely on the static `pkgver` variable. The top-level code contains only safe variable assignments. The `sha256sums_x86_64` array provides a valid checksum, meaning the source integrity will be verified after download. Even if it were 'SKIP', that would not make this step unsafe, as per the gate's criteria. No `prepare()`, `build()`, or `package()` execution occurs under `--noprepare` and `--nobuild`, so the `bsdtar` extraction logic is not reached during this phase.
</details>
<evidence>

</evidence>
<summary>
No malicious execution during source fetch and parse</summary>
</security_assessment>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file is a metadata file used by Arch Linux's AUR to describe the package and its sources. It does not contain executable code. The file specifies that the `codiff-bin` package is sourced from a prebuilt Debian package (`.deb`) hosted in the official GitHub releases of the project's upstream repository at `https://github.com/nkzw-tech/codiff`. The source URL points directly to versioned release assets (`v1.11.1`), which is consistent with standard packaging practices for binary packages.

The checksum provided (`sha256sums_x86_64`) matches the expected hash for the `.deb` file, indicating integrity verification will occur during package build. No skipped or missing checksums are present, so the source is verified. All dependencies listed are common system libraries (e.g., gtk3, nss, alsa-lib) typically required by GUI applications on Linux, and there are no unusual or suspicious runtime requirements.

There is no evidence of obfuscated URLs, dynamic downloads, or execution of fetched content in this file. Since `.SRCINFO` is declarative and cannot execute commands, and all referenced sources are from the legitimate upstream over HTTPS, the package appears safe from supply-chain tampering based on this metadata.
</details>
<evidence>

<summary>

</summary>
</security_assessment>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD retrieves a prebuilt Debian package from the project's official GitHub release page and extracts it using `bsdtar`. The source URL is over HTTPS and points to the legitimate upstream repository. The SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value for the release asset, ensuring integrity.

The package function extracts the contents of the `.deb` file in two stages: first reading the `data.tar.zst` from the Debian package, then extracting it directly into the package directory. This is a common and safe method when repackaging `.deb` files for Arch Linux. The script removes Debian-specific directories (`lintian`, `doc`) which is standard practice to avoid unnecessary files.

No obfuscated code, suspicious downloads, or unauthorized system modifications are present. The operations are limited to unpacking and permission adjustment, both within the build environment. All actions align with standard AUR packaging practices for binary packages.
</details>
